headline: CATTLE FLIP; GRAINS EASE AS HEAT EXITS BELT
subheadline: Feeders run 1.8% higher one session after their worst day in months, while corn and beans drift lower on favorable forecast.
lead: Feeders at $337.23, up 1.8% after getting worked over yesterday. The reversal is real but read it carefully: feedlot margins just turned negative per today's Drovers tracker, and the Cargill Fort Morgan lockout is still running. Yesterday's break may have been oversold. Today's bounce doesn't erase the structural problem.
the_takeaway: Feeders bounced hard, but negative feedlot margins say the ceiling is close.
teaser: Cattle flipped overnight; grains gave back more on a clearing weather map.

one_number.unit: feedlot margin dollars, turned negative today
one_number.context: Drovers' Profit Tracker posted negative feedlot margins this morning, the first read in the red in weeks. That cap on feeder demand is exactly why today's 1.8% bounce deserves skepticism even as the chart looks better.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called feeders down, below $328.00. Feeders closed today at $337.23, well above that line.
yesterdays_call.note: The break didn't materialize; feeders flipped the other direction entirely.

sections.title: Cattle Flip Overnight
sections.body:
- Feeders at **$337.23**, up 1.8% -- classic oversold snap-back after Monday's 3% break, not a fundamental turn.
- Drovers' margin tracker just went negative (see TMYK below): that is the ceiling on this bounce.
- Live cattle firmed to **$227.47**, up 1.2%, but the Cargill Fort Morgan lockout still removes roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity with no resolution in sight.
sections.bottom_line: Bounce is real, ceiling is close. Negative margins keep feeders from sustaining above $340.

sections.title: Grains Ease on Cooling Forecast
sections.body:
- Corn nearby at **$4.55**, off 4.25 cents; December at $4.77, off 3.75 cents as the Brownfield forecast pushes western Corn Belt heat out through the weekend.
- Beans slipped 9 cents to $11.98 nearby, giving back part of yesterday's technical bounce; a Missouri farmer's field report shows pods filling well heading into August, which is exactly what this market doesn't need for a weather premium.
- No clean catalyst beyond the forecast clearing; any weather premium that was left in corn pollination prices is walking out the door with the heat.
sections.catalyst: Brownfield: western Corn Belt heat exits by end of week; Missouri pod-fill reports positive.
sections.bottom_line: Corn's pollination window closing clean. Weather premium deflating, not building.
sections.vs_yesterday: Grains: technical bounce from Monday faded as forecast improved.

sections.title: Crude Firms on Middle East
sections.body:
- WTI at **$84.17**, up 1.8%, after the API reported a crude inventory draw and Houthi forces claimed a fresh attack on a Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea overnight.
- Iran-Hormuz tensions, with the Strait of Hormuz premium that built since early April now deflating on diplomatic progress, ran into a complication: Iran rejected Oman's proposal to share Hormuz control, and the UAE's ADNOC kept LNG exports moving through the Strait regardless.
- A planned $5 billion U.S.-Saudi refinery outside Hormuz signals long-term supply-chain hedging; diesel and fuel input costs for producers should track this closely.
sections.catalyst: Houthi attack claim on Saudi tanker; API crude draw; Iran rejects Hormuz-sharing proposal.
sections.bottom_line: Middle East noise is back in crude. Fuel input costs for fall fieldwork just ticked higher.

outside_the_pit.title: Congress Heads to Recess with $12 Billion Farm Aid Still Unsettled
outside_the_pit.body: The National Cotton Council says farm economic aid remains unresolved as Congress breaks for August. No distribution framework means producers waiting on relief checks should plan cash flow without that money landing before September at the earliest.

outside_the_pit.title: Senators Warn USDA Rural Development Reorganization Cuts Access
outside_the_pit.body: A Senate letter flagged that USDA's proposed Rural Development reorganization could strip small businesses and rural communities of services. Producers using USDA loan or business programs should verify their local office status before the restructuring moves forward.

weekly_thread.question: Will today's USDA crop progress ratings confirm the heat premium in beans, or reset grains lower?
weekly_thread.status_text: The heat is exiting the Belt per Brownfield's forecast, and Missouri pod-fill reports are positive; the premium is deflating, not building, as corn and beans drift lower Wednesday.

the_more_you_know.title: Negative Feedlot Margins: The Number That Caps the Bounce
the_more_you_know.body: When feedlot margins turn negative, packers and feeders stop competing aggressively for placement cattle. Today's Drovers tracker flip to negative is why $337 needs scrutiny: the bid dries up when feeding loses money. Watch whether cash cattle trade resets that math or confirms it.

watch_list.desc: USDA Weekly Export Sales: beans under 300K MT keeps chart in charge of price; above 600K MT reopens the $12.20 conversation.
Cargill Fort Morgan lockout resolution watch: any deal restores 6,000 head daily, pressures feeder prices back toward $330.
USDA Crop Progress: corn good/excellent below 60% would rebuild weather premium fast heading into August fill; above 65% seals the lid.
WTI above $85 puts diesel back in the farm input cost conversation for fall fieldwork; watch the Houthi-Saudi tanker story for follow-on moves.

daily_quote.text: A man of words and not of deeds is like a garden full of weeds.

source_summary: CME Group closing prices; USDA Crop Progress; Drovers Profit Tracker; Brownfield Ag News weather forecast; OilPrice.com (API draw, Houthi tanker attack, Iran/Oman Hormuz talks, ADNOC LNG); Feedstuffs (Senate USDA RD letter); Brownfield Ag News (farm aid, Missouri field report, fuel costs).
